title: [16/9/2024] The percentage of young people who were employed in different sectors in one country
prompt: The table shows the percentage of young people who were employed in different sectors in one country in 2005 and 2010. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the percentages of young people employed in various sectors in a country in two years, 2005 and 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while employment figures in social services, manufacturing, and transport decreased over the five-year period, there were increases in the percentages of young people working in agriculture, business, shops, restaurants and hotels, and other sectors. Additionally, social services, and shops, restaurants and hotels were the sectors with the highest percentages of young employees in 2010.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the sectors with the highest employment rates, social services accounted for 34% of young workers in 2005, followed by manufacturing and the hospitality industry, at approximately 20% each. By 2010, the manufacturing and social service sectors witnessed a notable decrease, falling to 22% and 14%, respectively. Meanwhile, the figure for shops, restaurants and hotels rose substantially to 32%, making it the sector with the highest proportion of young workers.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining sectors, business and other industries each accounted for less than 10% of young workers in 2005, at 7% and 8% respectively, while both agriculture and transport recorded the lowest proportions at 5%. Five years later, modest increases were seen in most of these sectors, with the percentages in business and other sectors reaching 10%, and agriculture rising to 8%. Transport was the only field that showed a slight decrease, dropping to 4%.
